goal: Help node operators identify peers that consume disproportionate CPU time during message processing
Assist in detecting abusive peers and evaluating future peer-scheduling policies
reviewability: Paused: waiting on author response to open design and interface objections from ajtowns and sipa
agreement: Unaddressed objection: per-peer CPU metrics are not actionable or comparable (ajtowns)
Unaddressed objection: belongs in an experimental RPC with decaying averages (sipa)
Objection: metric is useless without transaction acceptance context (rebroad)
Concept approval as a helpful first step for DoS mitigation (jonatack, laanwj, mzumsande)
Verified by testing on macOS and Ubuntu Signet IBD (jonatack, yuvicc, BrandonOdiwuor)

categories.name: rpc
why: P3 because it adds an unrequested diagnostic field to monitor peer CPU consumption
It offers modest observability for detecting DoS attacks but is reasonably deferrable

categories.name: utils
why: P3 because it adds reusable per-thread CPU timing utilities to support peer diagnostics
The cross-platform timing helpers are well defined but have low urgency on their own
